summary: Feed s153_double to IDS is degraded: 23.2% duplicate packets and 44.0% one-way TCP sessions. IDS requires bidirectional, deduplicated traffic for stateful inspection - both faults severely reduce detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding duplicate copies of same packets to the IDS - typically caused by aggregating two SPAN/mirror sessions or dual TAP feeds covering same link without deduplication, or a loop in aggregation. 452 of 1949 packets (23.2%) are duplicates vs 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes 1G capacity processing duplicates, inflates flow counts, causes signature engine to see retransmits/phantom packets, increases false positives and risks missing real threats due to processing overhead.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication on the feed to drop identical packets within a short time window before delivery to IDS, restoring accurate packet counts and freeing IDS resources for real traffic.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of TCP sessions is reaching the IDS - 51 of 116 sessions (44.0%) are one-way. Indicates asymmetric routing with TAP/SPAN on single side, or broker load-balancing / filtering that splits client->server and server->client to different tools without symmetric aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP reassembly and signature matching. With one-way visibility it cannot reconstruct streams, misses exploits that span request/response, fails to detect C2 and exfiltration, and generates incomplete session logs.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to aggregate both directions of each 5-tuple to this same IDS port using symmetric hashing, ensuring complete bidirectional flows for stateful detection.
